page: Microsoft Azure EC64es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by dedicated Intel Xeon processors. The instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Supporting the compute subsystem is a large cache hierarchy featuring 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, along with hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX tile and int8 extensions.

The server delivers 512.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. It features no local ephemeral disk storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities. The platform does not incorporate discrete graphics processing units. In synthetic stress-ng benchmarks, the machine achieves average single-core CPU throughput of 1922.78 and strong multi-core performance measuring 62306.6, placing it in the top quartile of multi-threaded compute.

Memory throughput and transactional capabilities are highlighted by Redis SET operations reaching 80.02 million operations per second, ranking within the top 25% of tested systems. Given its heavy memory footprint and dedicated multi-core capacity, the EC64es_v6 offers strong density for high-throughput in-memory caching systems, distributed enterprise databases, and transactional data processing environments that require extensive working memory without local scratch disks.
description: Microsoft Azure EC64es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by a dedicated 64-vCPU Intel Xeon processor architecture spanning 32 physical cores at 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation suitable for data-intensive processing. The instance features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512, without integrated GPUs or local drive storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves strong multi-threaded execution with a stress-ng score of 62306.6 and strong in-memory key-value processing at 80.02 million Redis SET operations per second, while single-core compute performance remains average. Because persistent storage relies entirely on external Premium Storage, the platform is targeted specifically at memory-resident workloads, including large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise in-memory databases, and high-concurrency transactional processing systems requiring broad RAM capacity and consistent thread scaling.
